title: 05 Conic sections: Visual Guide
outline: 1. From Circle To Ellipse | the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1 stretched by sliders a and b, with one point carried across by dashed arrows and the standard equation rewritten live | every ellipse is the unit circle scaled by a in x and b in y, which is why the plus sign means ellipse, why a = b is a circle, and why the right-hand side must be 1 before any denominator can be read

2. Sum Or Difference | a point dragged along an ellipse or a hyperbola with both focal distances drawn, printed and shown as bars, one of which never changes length | the ellipse pins the SUM of the two distances at 2a and the hyperbola pins their DIFFERENCE at 2a, and because the foci are inside a closed ellipse but outside the hyperbola's vertices, c is smaller than a for one and larger for the other

3. Foci Vertices Axes | the two denominators set by sliders, with vertices, foci, eccentricity and the amber right triangle (or central rectangle) that derives c drawn on the curve | for an ellipse a is the larger denominator and c^2 = a^2 - b^2, for a hyperbola a is whichever sits under the plus sign and c^2 = a^2 + b^2, and vertices are +/-a rather than +/-a^2

4. Name That Conic | seven equations classified live from their coefficients through a three-question ladder, then plotted in a window you can widen to x = 40 | both variables squared with the same sign is an ellipse (equal is a circle), opposite signs a hyperbola, one squared variable a parabola — and zooming out shows the difference that matters: bounded, hugging an asymptote of slope b/a, or outrunning every line
